title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) to measure how often LLM-produced network-configuration proposals would cause unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action) and whether an automated defended pipeline reduces that rate versus an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks (planned 600 paired episodes), executed paired baseline and guarded conditions, and archived every raw response, provider trace, per-episode scoring JSON, and validator trace with full SHA‑256 provenance. After applying preregistered missingness rules the primary analysis used 272 complete pairs: n11=271, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0 (baseline safe rate = 271/272 = 0.99632; guarded safe rate = 272/272 = 1.00000; paired absolute difference = 0.003676470588235281; paired‑bootstrap 95% percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). A verified execution deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage did not execute (execution manifest documents stage_counts and call audit), so the archived guarded condition corresponds to deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to the shared single generation; the preregistered ensemble hypothesis therefore remains untested in this run. We report exact archived counts, provide artifact paths and SHA‑256s for deterministic verification, discuss orchestration and validation lessons, and identify reproducibility steps for an ensemble re‑execution.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLMs for NetOps map natural‑language intent into concrete configuration actions. When model text becomes state‑changing tool calls or device configuration, fluent but incorrect claims can trigger harmful changes — a claim→action failure surface distinct from text‑level hallucination. Prior work recommends generate–validate–repair pipelines, deterministic verification (header‑space/SMT/NetKAT family), ensembles/consensus gating, and human gates. We preregistered a paired, confirmatory measurement to (1) quantify claim→action rates for intent→configuration tasks under an unguarded baseline and (2) estimate the guarded pipeline’s reduction in unsafe simulated deployments. We archived every artifact and followed a frozen preregistration (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26, preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). The primary estimand is the paired absolute difference in per-task safe‑execution rate: safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline.
sections.related_work: Deterministic validators and symbolic network verification give operationally meaningful safety predicates that are used here as the scoring oracle. Recent LLM‑for‑NetOps and AIOps literature demonstrate tool‑augmented agents, validator‑guided repair, and ensemble gating as defenses; our contribution is an artifact‑anchored preregistered paired measurement with per‑episode deterministic validator traces and full SHA‑256 provenance to permit independent re‑verification.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistration (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) specified a paired binary design, planned 300 tasks (100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial planned) producing 600 episodes, primary estimand paired difference in safe rates on complete pairs, exact McNemar two‑sided confirmatory test, and paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for CI. Task generation and simulator. A deterministic generator produced synthetic intent→configuration tasks with explicit workflow constraints (must‑be‑down rules, minimum‑up invariants, required ordered sequences). Validator and scoring. We used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the adjudicator; every per‑episode scoring JSON contains the validator_trace (parsed command counts, touched fields, simulated final state, explicit violation codes, normalized configuration). Execution and provenance. Orchestration, all provider traces, raw responses, scoring JSONs, and validator traces are archived; execution/execution_manifest.json records per‑file SHA‑256s and provider‑call audit (model_calls_used, completed/failed counts, stage_counts). Missingness, retries, and sensitivity. One automatic retry per failed model call was permitted; episodes with unresolved provider failures were treated per the preregistered missingness rules (complete‑pair primary analysis; preregistered conservative sensitivity treats failed episodes as unsafe). All artifacts and manifest hashes are archived for deterministic reproducibility.
sections.results: Execution accounting and artifacts. Planned episodes = 600 (paired design); completed episodes = 544; failed episodes = 56. Provider audit (execution/execution_manifest.json): model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28. Complete analyzable pairs = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = 682a629aee104ef5c3d3b3e494f881ca05fa38bc10831e1f7c9164c70c754c27). Primary paired contingency (complete pairs N=272): n11 = 271 (safe both), n10 = 1 (safe baseline only), n01 = 0 (safe guarded only), n00 = 0 (unsafe both). Observed safe rates: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.003676470588235281. Paired‑bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729): [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Conservative preregistered sensitivity (treat the 28 failed provider calls as unsafe on planned N=300) yields baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333 and guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667 (difference = 0.0033333333). Representative artifacts. Example per‑episode scoring JSONs and response texts are archived and hashed (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = 465d73fd..., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = b227731a...; execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 = 8f38c8be...).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and operational meaning. Under the executed pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation), the guarded condition showed near‑perfect acceptance on analyzable pairs, but the paired improvement over baseline is extremely small and statistically inconclusive in this run. Crucially, a verified execution deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage did not run (the execution manifest documents stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300, "repair":1} and condition_counts indicating the ensemble stage absence). Therefore this run cannot test the preregistered ensemble hypothesis; any ensemble claim requires re‑execution with hardened orchestration so the ensemble stage actually executes. Sources of uncertainty and threats. (1) Orchestration fragility: 28 failed provider calls materially reduced effective N and power; robust retry/backoff, deterministically paged caching, and active monitoring are needed for ensemble evaluation. (2) Construct validity: synthetic intent→configuration tasks and deterministic simulator capture operational invariants but are not a substitute for vendor hardware/production traffic. (3) External validity: single declared model (gpt-5-mini) — no multi‑model generality supported by this run. (4) Missing preregistered summary artifact: the preregistration required reporting realized prompt‑family counts (benign/ambiguous/adversarial) for (a) planned N=300 tasks, (b) the analyzable complete pairs N=272, and (c) the 28 failed episodes. These counts can be deterministically computed from the archived execution/task_manifest.jsonl artifact (canonical path: execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = 3d7b63c361c9848b20750cc44125f195f0341346d48393ce72ae07d6c0fea745). The assembled high‑level analysis outputs included in this manuscript did not contain a separate per‑family summary file; therefore we did not re‑open or re‑parse execution/task_manifest.jsonl during final composition to avoid post‑analysis edits. The canonical artifact path and SHA‑256 permit an independent verifier or the authors to compute exact per‑family realized counts from the archived manifest; future runs should include an explicit per‑family analysis output to avoid this gap. Reproducibility and verification. Minimal artifacts to reproduce the primary contingency are archived with SHA‑256s: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 682a629aee104ef5c3d3b3e494f881ca05fa38bc10831e1f7c9164c70c754c27), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b48494c4014de396afb395e78e227f827abc35f1777c23fa25b67b1d20d6f408), analysis/missingness_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 97bde3aef2ce7228e290a8102ad97079586654c1fe512046d109268c93eae2c6), and the full execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) that lists every archived file and per‑file SHA‑256. Operational recommendations. (1) Harden orchestration (deterministic caching, robust retry/backoff, live stage monitoring) before ensemble experiments. (2) Continue using deterministic validators that produce auditable validator_traces for per‑episode deterministic adjudication. (3) Publish an explicit per‑family summary artifact alongside the analyses to satisfy preregistered reporting requirements.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed an artifact‑anchored paired measurement to quantify claim→action risk and evaluate an automated guard. The executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation) achieved near‑perfect analyzable‑pair acceptance, but the preregistered ensemble hypothesis was not executed due to an orchestration deviation. All per‑episode artifacts and an exhaustive per‑file SHA‑256 manifest are archived to permit deterministic verification and re‑execution; a re‑run with hardened orchestration is required to evaluate the preregistered ensemble defense fully.

limitations: Single declared model present in the archived execution (declared model = "gpt-5-mini"); no multi-model generality claims are supported by this run.
Synthetic tasks and a deterministic simulator were used; construct and external validity versus vendor hardware and production environments are limited.

A verified execution deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage did not run; the archived guarded condition therefore evaluates a different pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation).
Provider call failures (28 failed hosted model calls) reduced the effective sample and limited power to detect small absolute effects.
